# Certification of an electronic record — template (FRE 902(13) / 902(14) model)

> **Not legal advice.** This is a blank template. `agentdfir export custody --certify`
> fills the case facts (digests, rounds, dates, tool version) from the sealed
> package and leaves every `[[ ]]` field for a qualified person to complete and
> sign. The tool never signs on anyone's behalf. Whether such a certification is
> accepted is a question for a court and for counsel in your jurisdiction.

US Federal Rules of Evidence 902(13) and 902(14) (both effective 2017-12-01)
let certain electronic records be *self-authenticating* on the written
certification of a qualified person: 902(13) for a record generated by an
electronic process or system, and 902(14) for data copied from an electronic
device and identified by a process such as a hash. Self-authentication is about
whether a record is what it claims to be; it is not a ruling on relevance,
hearsay or admissibility. Other jurisdictions apply different frameworks — for
example ISO/IEC 27037 for the identification, collection, acquisition and
preservation of digital evidence.

---

I, **[[ full name of the qualified person ]]**, **[[ title / qualification ]]**
at **[[ organization ]]**, declare the following of my own knowledge:

1. **Qualification.** I am qualified to make this certification because
   [[ state the basis: role, training, familiarity with the system and the
   collection process ]].

2. **The records.** This certification concerns the AgentDFIR evidence package
   for case **[[ case id ]]**, collected from host **[[ host ]]**, created
   **[[ creation time (UTC) ]]**.

3. **Generated by an electronic process (902(13)).** The records were produced
   by AI coding-agent software on the host in the normal course of its
   operation, and were read from the host by AgentDFIR version **[[ version ]]**
   (collector binary SHA-256 **[[ binary hash ]]**). AgentDFIR copies files
   without modifying them, records each artifact's SHA-256, and does not execute
   the software under investigation.

4. **Copied from an electronic device (902(14)).** Each artifact's `artifact_id`
   is the SHA-256 of its plaintext content, recorded at the time of copying. The
   complete sealed set is covered by a SHA-256 manifest (`SHA256SUMS`) whose own
   SHA-256 digest is **[[ seal digest ]]**. The package [[ is / is not ]] signed
   (ed25519, `SEAL.sig`); the signer key fingerprint is **[[ fingerprint ]]**.

5. **Collection.** The acquisition was carried out in **[[ N ]]** round(s), each
   recorded with its start and completion time, collector version and seal:
   [[ list the rounds, or let `export custody` fill them ]].

6. **Authority for the acquisition.** [[ state who authorized the acquisition
   and on what basis — recorded in the case with `agentdfir case authorize` ]].

7. **Integrity can be re-checked.** Anyone can confirm the package is unaltered
   by re-running `agentdfir verify` on it, or with standard tools:
   `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS` inside the package, and (if signed) ed25519
   verification of `SEAL.sig` against the manifest digest above. A single changed
   byte breaks the check.

8. **Scope and limits.** This certification concerns the integrity and provenance
   of the copied records. It does not opine on the meaning of their contents, on
   whether any action was authorized, or on any legal conclusion. The evidence
   shows what the host retained; it does not include vendor-side logs or anything
   deleted before collection.

Signed: ______________________________    Date: **[[ date ]]**

Printed name: **[[ full name ]]**
